events.title: The death of St. Columba of Iona
events.shortBlurb: The Irish monk who planted the faith among the Picts from his island monastery of Iona died among his brethren…
body: On 9 June 597 Columba — Colum Cille, 'the dove of the church' — died on Iona, in the monastery he had ruled for thirty-four years. Born about 521 at Gartan in Donegal, of the royal Uí Néill kindred, he had founded churches at Derry and Durrow before leaving Ireland.

In 563, after the battle of Cúl Dreimhne with which tradition links his departure, he crossed to Britain with twelve companions and received the island of Iona for his foundation. From its cloister he preached among the Picts, inaugurated Áedán mac Gabráin as king of the Scots of Dál Riata, and formed missionaries for all northern Britain.

His life was written within a century by his kinsman and successor Adomnán, whose Vita Columbae is the chief monument of the Celtic mission. Dying before the altar at the midnight office, he left a mother-house whose sons — Aidan of Lindisfarne among them — carried the Gospel into England; with Patrick and Brigid he is honored as a patron of Ireland.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 9 June
